targets.summary: This logic is duplicated elsewhere in the code; the other places should reuse this helper.
targets.evidence: The commented line `def surviving_sidecars(op: str, sidecars: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:` is the same in the merged code. Only its docstring changed, which now says "Idempotent, so a caller may filter and pass the result on." The other copy of this logic was in gen_op, which re-ran the survivor filter inline: before review it had `sidecars = [sc for scs in groups.values() for sc in scs]`. In the merged code that line is `sidecars = surviving_sidecars(op, sidecars)`, and its comment says "Through the helper main() uses -- it is idempotent, so filtering an already-filtered list is silent and cheap." So the duplicated code now calls the helper, which is what the maintainer asked for. The diff shows no other inline copies left.

targets.summary: Platform-specific handling looks unnecessary since this only runs on Linux; add an early exit for Windows/Apple instead.
targets.evidence: Before, the exclude-libs block had its own guard: `"if(UNIX AND NOT APPLE)",` wrapping `target_link_options(torch_cuda PRIVATE "SHELL:-Xlinker --exclude-libs ...")`. In the merged code that per-block guard is gone. CMAKE_DSL_RUNTIME_TMPL now emits `target_link_libraries(torch_cuda PRIVATE {runtime})` followed by `target_link_options(torch_cuda PRIVATE "SHELL:-Xlinker --exclude-libs -Xlinker \"{runtime_name}\"")` with no condition around it. A single early exit, CMAKE_PLATFORM_GUARD, was added near the top: `if(NOT UNIX OR APPLE)  message(STATUS "native-AOT: not Linux, not embedding kernels")  return() endif()`. Its comment says "Linux only, deliberately... One exit rather than a guard per linker block". This is the early exit for Windows/Apple that the maintainer asked for.
